reproduction.text: Live young, about 6 at a time

overview.text: The Rosy Boa is a small, calm boa of the deserts of the south-western United States and north-western Mexico. It is one of only a few boas native to the mainland United States.

identification.text: Usually three stripes (orange, tan, brown or pink) run down a pale body - 'trivirgata' means 'three-striped'. Colours vary a lot from place to place; some have a pink, rosy belly.

size.label: Adults
size.text: A small boa: even a big adult's body is only about as thick as a golf ball.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Southern California and south-western Arizona in the USA, and Baja California and western Sonora in Mexico.

habitat.text: Rocky deserts - most often granite outcrops. Where there are few rocks it hides in rodent burrows.

behaviour.text: Spends most of its life hidden under rocks and in cracks, away from heat and predators.

reproduction.text: Gives birth to live young, about six at a time; the babies can be up to 30 cm long.

recognise.text: Three long stripes down the body.
